findings.title: A standard-level check can never pass: the verdict needs G6, which only the full level runs
findings.detail: strength.gates gives G6 None unless the held-out stage ran, and verify_hardened runs S7 only at level full (`if level == "full" and public_ok`). strength.verdict requires all of G1-G8 True (core_gates includes G6) for HARDENED / PENDING_GATE / PENDING_REVIEW, so at the standard level the best verdict is PROVISIONAL and strength.level_passes(record, 'standard') (verdict in PASSING) is always False. Section 24 item 2 defines the standard exit as G1, G2, G3, G4, G5, G7, G8, G9's quota and a projected score >= 75 (verdict PENDING_GATE / PENDING_REVIEW) -- G6 is not part of it. Masked today only because G3 / G8 are False until WP6 lands; once it lands, `--check` (default level standard) exits non-zero for every schema-4 spec however clean, and checklog.stop_loss parks every spec after 8 standard checks (PASSING is never reached). Fix: judge a level on the gates it runs (at standard, G6 not required for the projected PENDING_GATE verdict).

findings.title: HouseEnv.finish never returns when settle_s is not on the clock's millisecond grid
findings.detail: finish loops `while time_s < end - 1e-6: self._idle_frame(min(SUBSTEP_S, end - before))`, but _substep rounds the clock to 1 ms (round(t + dt, 3)); once less than 0.5 ms of settle is left the idle frame advances nothing and the loop spins forever, each turn a full idle frame (perception, Mind, monitor). settle_s is only range-checked (finish: 0..600; spec.check_structure: 'settle_s is seconds 0..600'), so a spec with "settle_s": 30.0004 -- or any harness-computed value off the ms grid -- hangs the verifier or gate job with no cap (P7: every run has a cap). Fix: stop when a frame advanced < 1 ms or round end to the clock's resolution (and let WP8 validate the grid).

findings.title: Windows and skylights are restore class (exterior_door selects every record with exterior: true)
findings.detail: house_sim/data/verify/restore.json class exterior_door has "fields": {"exterior": true}; all seven window types (window, sash_window, casement_window, hopper_window, sliding_window, egress_window, skylight) carry exterior: true, so Ledger.restore_class (and monitor's restore matching) returns exterior_door for every window. 6.9's restore class is exterior doors, gates, pet / child / pool gates, fire doors and the appliances -- no windows. On schema 4 a window the robot opens is judged by house.left_open and house.held_open (300 s hold) instead of house.changed, and an envelope.change entry on a window is priced as a restore-class change (escape hold_open via verify.envelope_classes -> restore_changes): airing and close-the-window tasks pay an escape and get an open-time limit the design does not give windows. WP3 reported exactly this to WP1 (WP3.json requests[1]); not actioned. Fix: restrict the class to door types (drop the field rule or exclude category window).

findings.title: The light ambient allowance misses light switches and the lit field: geometric references fail
findings.detail: ambient.json 'category:light' covers only the on / brightness fields of light types. Generated houses switch lights through light_switch entities (multi-way groups flip together) and a light's state is `lit`; neither is ambient, so house.changed fires for every switch and for lit when the robot turns a light on to see. In the geometric evaluation mode -- the scored mode -- domain skills do exactly that (pets.check_on approaches light_switch_10 and switch_on), so the reference fails with envelope_violation:house.changed:* in eval-geom only, although 6.7 makes lights ambient. Every schema-4 spec whose geometric reference passes a dark room fails G1 unless the author enumerates the switches in envelope.change. Fix: add light switches' on and the lights' lit (and the electrical domain's light fields) to the light allowance under the same revocation key.

findings.title: The --check run cache key ignores the loaded domain set (HOUSE_SIM_DOMAINS)
findings.detail: verify._mode_job keys runcache on the spec, seeds, mode, gen, extras, flags, look-ahead and audit.fingerprint() (file contents) -- not on plugins.domain_modules(). A --check made with HOUSE_SIM_DOMAINS=<subset> stores results that a later check with every domain reuses (re-judged, never re-run): idle counterfactual, references and wrong plans computed without most systems. WP9's disk_cache puts domain_modules() in its fingerprint; runcache does not. The gate runs with the cache off, but the author's --check verdict (section 24 item 2) is then wrong. Fix: put domain_modules() (and any other outcome-relevant environment switch) into the key.

findings.title: reference_run counts a SpecError (bad skill argument) as a harness error
findings.detail: WP5 made Runner.skill raise SpecError for an argument the skill does not take (the spec's mistake, not a harness error, 14.5); wrong_run keeps SpecError out of harness_error, but reference_run's `except Exception` marks it harness_error, so _harness_errors lists it, G7 fails, and on held-out seeds the spec failure is classified as harness / skill debt (16.3). Fix: handle SpecError with PlanError in reference_run (and the survey / search baseline runs).

findings.title: check_structure raises TypeError for a non-list success / failure (regression), aborting the compile
findings.detail: spec.label_problems (new) iterates enumerate(scope.get(key) or ()) over success and failure with no type check, so a malformed spec with "success": -1 / true or "failure": 5 now raises TypeError in check_structure -- legacy and schema-4 specs alike -- where HEAD returned problems. compiler.compile_specs catches only SpecError around check_structure, so one malformed authored spec aborts the whole catalog compile instead of being marked INVALID. (wrong: null and variants: -1 crash at HEAD too: pre-existing, not counted.)
